title: The Tower of Babel and the Family of Abram

verses.1: At that time the whole earth had one language and everyone used the same words.
verses.2: As people migrated from the east, they found a flat plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.
verses.3: They said to one another, "Come, let us make bricks and bake them hard." They used bricks instead of stone and bitumen instead of mortar.
verses.4: Then they said, "Come, let us build a city with a tower that reaches up to the sky. We will make a great name for ourselves and not be scattered over the whole earth."
verses.5: The LORD came down to see the city and the tower that the people were building.
verses.6: The LORD said, "They are one people with one language. This is only the beginning of what they will do. Nothing they plan will be too difficult for them.
verses.7: Come, let Us go down and mix up their language so they cannot understand each other."
verses.8: So the LORD scattered them from there over all the earth, and they stopped building the city.
verses.9: That is why the city was named Babel — because there the LORD confused the language of the whole earth. From there the LORD scattered them over the face of all the earth.
verses.10: These are the family records of Shem. When Shem was 100 years old, he fathered Arpachshad, two years after the flood.
verses.11: After he fathered Arpachshad, Shem lived 500 more years and had other sons and daughters.
verses.12: When Arpachshad had lived 35 years, he fathered Shelah.
verses.13: After he fathered Shelah, Arpachshad lived 403 more years and had other sons and daughters.
verses.14: When Shelah had lived 30 years, he fathered Eber.
verses.15: After he fathered Eber, Shelah lived 403 more years and had other sons and daughters.
verses.16: When Eber had lived 34 years, he fathered Peleg.
verses.17: After he fathered Peleg, Eber lived 430 more years and had other sons and daughters.
verses.18: When Peleg had lived 30 years, he fathered Reu.
verses.19: After he fathered Reu, Peleg lived 209 more years and had other sons and daughters.
verses.20: When Reu had lived 32 years, he fathered Serug.
verses.21: After he fathered Serug, Reu lived 207 more years and had other sons and daughters.
verses.22: When Serug had lived 30 years, he fathered Nahor.
verses.23: After he fathered Nahor, Serug lived 200 more years and had other sons and daughters.
verses.24: When Nahor had lived 29 years, he fathered Terah.
verses.25: After he fathered Terah, Nahor lived 119 more years and had other sons and daughters.
verses.26: After Terah had lived 70 years, he fathered Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
verses.27: These are the family records of Terah. Terah was the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran was the father of Lot.
verses.28: Haran died while his father Terah was still alive, in the land where he was born — Ur of the Chaldeans.
verses.29: Abram and Nahor both married. Abram's wife was named Sarai, and Nahor's wife was named Milcah. Milcah was the daughter of Haran, who was also the father of Iscah.
verses.30: Sarai was not able to have children.
verses.31: Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot, who was the son of Haran, and his daughter-in-law Sarai, the wife of Abram. Together they left Ur of the Chaldeans to travel to the land of Canaan. But when they came to Haran, they stopped and settled there.
verses.32: Terah lived 205 years, and he died in Haran.

metadata.source: Based on the Authorized King James Version (1769), reinterpreted through the theology of abiding in Christ.
